text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Elevated 5xx + timeouts observed from inference-gateway -> private backends (prod-private-vpc). Alerting threshold breached (5xx rate > 8% for 3m). Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/board/inf-gw-prod (pager triggered)

oncall-eng: got the page, I'm on it. starting initial triage.

sre-maya: digging into logs now. 502/504s appear across multiple AZs but concentrated for customer accounts in VPC peered workspace `corp-prod`.

eng-runtime-ben: are these backend pods healthy? can we see pod-level 5xx?

sre-maya: pod health looks OK. Backend app logs show connection resets and socket timeouts when gateway attempts upstream connect. Not typical app error.

netops-alex: I'm seeing a sharp drop in outbound flows from the private subnets to the NAT. NAT metrics show SNAT port exhaustion and elevated connection errors.

infra-raj: which NAT type? managed NAT GW or instance?

netops-alex: this tenant is using a shared NAT instance (old stack) with dynamic SNAT ports per ENI. Conntrack table size jumped. If NAT can't allocate ephemeral ports, upstream connections fail -> 502/504 at gateway.

oncall-eng: can we confirm scope? number of customers impacted? severity?

custsuccess-anna: reached out to the CSM for corp-prod; they report degraded inference latencies and some 5xx responses in production — a few paying customers impacted. Need ETA/comm.

eng-runtime-ben: temporary mitigation: can we route this vpc's egress through a different NAT (fallback) or short-circuit to hosted inference for affected tenants?

netops-alex: options: 1) scale NAT (add another NAT instance + update route table), 2) switch them to a managed NAT gateway with larger port space, 3) enable source-NAT on per-ENI (if supported), 4) reduce TTL for long-lived connections / enable connection reuse. Fastest is add a second NAT instance and update route table association to balance.

oncall-eng: do it. Alex, please create the new NAT and associate route table. Raj, coordinate EIP assignment. Ben, prepare runtime fallback config if we need to flip routes to hosted.

netops-alex: creating NAT instance now. attaching EIP. will update route table association in ~3m.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: NAT instance creation request submitted by netops-alex.

sre-maya: adding temporary alert mute for noisy downstream error sources while we remediate (muting per-tenant alert).

custsuccess-anna: telling impacted customers: "We're seeing transient 5xx/timeouts affecting private VPC inference for some workloads. Our engineers are actively remediating and will follow up with an incident summary."

product-liz: please capture any customer-visible error messages and affected endpoints — product will prepare follow-up comms.

netops-alex: route table updated, traffic starts moving to new NAT. Monitoring shows immediate decrease in connection errors; SNAT port usage back to normal range.

eng-runtime-ben: I see reduced 502s but some timeouts persist for long-lived sockets. Could be stale connection tracking entries on the NAT.

netops-alex: I'm forcing conntrack cleanup on the instance and restarting the NAT forwarding agent.

`netstat -an | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l` output before: 49200
`conntrack -L | wc -l` before: 138k

netops-alex: cleared ~90k conntrack entries, forcing re-establish.

sre-maya: error rate now down to ~0.8% across the fleet for this tenant. Still watching for full recovery.

eng-runtime-ben: added short-term client-side retry for 502 with 100ms jitter to ease bursts. Also lowered upstream idle timeout from 120s -> 30s to avoid leaked sockets. Rolling now.

incident-bot: NOTE: oncall handoff required in 30m. current lead: oncall-eng. next: oncall-eng (same rotation) but netops oncall will retain ownership until confirmed stable.

custsuccess-anna: AB contacted customers; they're requesting formal RCA and whether any data loss. We confirmed no user data lost; requests were retried/failed but not persisted.

product-liz: flagging this for post-incident review: private NAT instance designs across older tenants are single point failures; we need a migration plan to managed NAT GW or per-tenant managed egress.

infra-raj: follow-up actions tracked: 1) migrate corp-prod to managed NAT gateway (ticket INF-2234), 2) add conntrack tuning and alert for >70% port usage (SRE-431), 3) add automated fallback to hosted inference for private-vpc on severe egress failures (PROD-88), 4) run retro and hit list.

netops-alex: making NAT instance immutable snapshot & configuration doc. will keep instance until migration completes.

sre-maya: closing incident once 24h of stable metrics. setting check at +24h.

oncall-eng: handing over to netops-alex for monitoring and ticketing. I'm marking the incident as mitigated. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

netops-alex: taking post-incident owner. will update ticket INF-2234 with timeline and steps.

product-liz: please add customer comms draft to the ticket.

custsuccess-anna: will send customer follow-up with root-cause summary and planned mitigations in the next 2 hours.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigated — egress NAT port exhaustion remediated via added NAT instance + conntrack cleanup. Severity: Sev2 -> Monitoring.

sre-maya: final note — recommend we scan other legacy VPCs for shared NAT instances and prioritize migrations.

eng-runtime-ben: also recommended we add upstream connection pooling improvements to reduce ephemeral port consumption. Filed runtime ticket RUN-556.

noncall-eng: thanks team. I'll close the chat once postmortem notes are in the ticket.

netops-alex: timeline (short):
- 1794023401: alert fired (5xx spike)
- 1794023430: netops triage — identified NAT port exhaustion
- 1794023505: new NAT instance created + EIP attached
- 1794023531: route table updated -> traffic flows to new NAT
- 1794023600: conntrack cleanup + NAT agent restart
- 1794023720: error rate down to baseline
- 1794023987: incident marked mitigated, handoff to netops for remediation ticketing

incident-bot: Logging incident summary and creating incident#INC-1794023401 in tracker.

custsuccess-anna: copying final comms to channel: "Root cause: SNAT/conntrack exhaustion on a shared NAT instance in private VPC after increased concurrency. Mitigation: added NAT capacity and flushed connection tracking. No customer data loss. Next steps: migration to managed NAT, conntrack alarms, runtime pooling improvements."

product-liz: good work. we'll schedule a 1-hour postmortem tomorrow.

sre-maya: monitoring link: https://grafana.redwood/board/inf-gw-prod — keep an eye but looks stable.

end of thread.
